correctness.rationale: All six facet distances, including the vertical half-height, are fixed at one; 0 <= c < 1 parametrizes that family up to congruence. The first pedal is the polar with exactly eight supporting planes indexed by the sign vectors; the second feet are their dual sign vectors divided by squared norm. In the orthogonal horizontal sum/difference axes the resulting four columns have radii A,B and half-heights h+,h−. A supporting functional of the projected diamond, slightly tilted vertically, exposes each endpoint. In any convex representation the total weight at the two Y-corners is at least |Y|/B, and this lower bound can be attained throughout the diamond; placing all mass on the upper endpoints therefore yields the claimed roof for h+ >= h−. This proves the four lateral quadrilaterals and four roof triangles for c>0 (two merged flat roofs at c=0). Section integration gives V=4AB(2h++h−)/3. Differentiation gives the stated quintic and positive prefactor; F′(c) <= 99(c−1)<0 before the excluded endpoint. Opposite endpoint signs and the rational bracket establish the unique interior global maximum; the cube gives 8/27, and V tends to zero as c approaches 1. An exact determinant test at c=3/5 gave 190/729 without floating hull triangulation, and the derivative replay reproduced c*=0.175097381279917 and V*=0.302143544127582.
residual_risks: The rational hull test is corroboration only. The proof does not address arbitrary prism heights, sheared axes, or unnormalized or uncircumscribed parallelotopes.

Same-day rigidity theorem and bicentric-prism theorem for the narrower known conclusions
value.rationale: A single natural shape parameter ranges from the symmetric cube to near-degeneracy while all facet distances are fixed. The calculation gives a sharp counterexample to cube extremality on this family, a complete facet transition, and a unique maximizing geometry. The value is the structural comparison and exact optimizer, not the size of the percentage gain.
residual_risks: This is a one-parameter classification, not an extremum theorem over all circumscribed polytopes or all prisms.
